subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & next steps — Atlas Payments

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Thanks for walking through the fraud-detection use case — notes and proposed plan below.

Recap (call highlights)
- Objective: Replace current heuristic pipeline with a low-latency ranking+rerank model for transaction risk signals.
- Key integrations: streaming transaction events, real-time lookups to internal features, and batch re-eval for tuning.
- Initial scope: evaluate Redwood hosted inference with a 4-week POC.

Proposed POC success criteria / KPIs (please confirm or adjust)
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency <= 200ms for 1-2k token prompts (target: 150ms).
2) Throughput: sustained 250 concurrent inference requests with tail latency SLOs met.
3) Cost: amortized cost per token <= $0.002 (target for budgeting).
4) Quality: top-3 precision/recall on labeled test set >= 90% (we'll agree on a representative eval set).
5) Reliability: 99.9% availability during business hours; graceful fallback to smaller model if needed.

Evaluation plan (draft)
- Week 0: onboarding + baseline data exchange (you provide sample event stream and labeled evaluation set).
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests with small traffic.
- Week 2: scale tests (load & latency profiling).
- Week 3: quality validation on labeled set + iteration.
- Week 4: wrap-up, results review, and recommendation.

Ownership (suggested)
- Atlas: provide labeled evaluation dataset, internal SRE contact for traffic routing, test accounts.
- Redwood: Jordan (AM) — program lead; Rishi (SE) — technical lead for benchmarking; Laura (CS) — onboarding and runbook.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the KPIs above (latency/throughput/cost/quality) or propose adjustments?
2) Please share the labeled evaluation set and a short sample of the production event stream (PII redacted) — we can take SFTP or Drive.
3) I'll share the POC scope workbook and test-plan checklist (attached) and a HubSpot deal link for tracking.

Attachments: redwood-poc-scope.xlsx, poc-testplan-checklist.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick sync if you'd like to adjust targets.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and proposed plan. Quick answers from our side:

Confirmed KPIs (with minor adjustments)
- Latency: 95th <= 180ms (our internal target is 150ms but let's set 180ms as the POC acceptance threshold).
- Throughput: sustain 300 concurrent QPS during spike windows (critical for peak-hour volume).
- Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0025 (we can optimize later; finance needs a slightly higher threshold for now).
- Quality: Top-3 precision >= 88% on our labeled fraud confirmation set (we can share the labels).
- Reliability: 99.95% during business-critical windows.

Timeline
- We are aiming to start the POC week of Apr 5 and complete by May 3. That gives us ~4 weeks of active testing with time for legal/ops to clear.

Stakeholders
- Alyssa Chen (product lead) — me
- Tom Ruiz (engineering lead) — will share an SRE contact for routing
- I'll loop in procurement for standard terms; expect NDA signed this week.

Deliverables we'll share this week
- Labeled evaluation set (CSV)
- Sample event stream (sanitized)
- Procurement contact email

Looks good — please update the workbook to reflect the adjusted thresholds and confirm timeline.

Thanks,

Hi team — jumping in with the technical evaluation plan and acceptance criteria details. Appreciate the targets Alyssa called out; I've translated them into measurable tests below.

Measurement methodology
- Latency: measure end-to-end 95p using our load harness (realistic batching and token distributions). We'll report both model inference time and end-to-end time including network/service overhead.
- Throughput: ramp to sustained 300 concurrent requests with a 5% allowed error rate on 95p latency. We'll run repeated 1hr soak tests at target concurrency.
- Cost: track token-in/token-out across the test runs and compute amortized cost per token (we'll model real traffic mix to estimate).
- Quality: hold-out labeled set (we'll use the CSV you'll provide). Evaluate top-3 precision and recall and compute a pass/fail against 88% precision. We'll also surface model-level failure modes (hallucination, truncation).

Test plan (high level)
- Day 0 (pre-kickoff): confirm data shapes and sanitization method for your sample stream.
- Week 1: integration + small-scale smoke tests (up to 50rps).
- Week 2: scale tests to 300 concurrent; collect latency profiles and KV/cache hit rates.
- Week 3: quality eval + A/B runs between model variants (quantized vs full-precision).
- Week 4: final report, regression notes, and cost model.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail)
- Latency: 95p end-to-end <= 180ms — PASS
- Throughput: 300 concurrent with 95p <= 180ms and <=5% error budget — PASS
- Cost: modeled amortized cost/token <= $0.0025 — PASS
- Quality: top-3 precision >= 88% on agreed test set — PASS

Artifacts I'll deliver
- Benchmark harness (link to drive) + docker image for local runs
- Benchmark report with percentile breakdowns, flamegraphs, and recommendations (kernel/quant config)
- Final cost model spreadsheet and recommended deployment profile (dedicated vs hosted)

Attachments: poc-testplan-checklist.pdf
